prerequisites: The TFG must be defended and evaluated once it is reliably confirmed that the student has passed all remaining subjects of the study plan and therefore has all the necessary credits for obtaining the Degree title, except those corresponding to the TFG itself.

learning_outcomes.text: The Final Degree Project is an original exercise, to be carried out individually or in a group, which must be presented and defended individually before a university tribunal. It consists of carrying out a project in the field of the specific technology of the Degree title studied, of a professional nature, in which the competencies acquired in the teachings are synthesized and integrated.

In the development of the final degree project, the student will generally work on all the general competencies of the degree, from CG1 to CG15. Also, depending on the topic of the work, various specific competencies will be addressed. Specifically, in compliance with O.M. CIN/351/2009, it must be a work in which the competencies acquired in the teachings are synthesized and integrated: TFG Competence.

The specific learning outcomes of the final degree project will vary depending on the topic assigned by the tutor but, as a general rule, will be directly related to the specific objectives of the degree. These results will be reflected in the individual or group realization of the work, individual presentation and defense before a university tribunal of an original project in the field of Engineering of a professional nature, and in which all acquired competencies are synthesized and integrated.

syllabus_topics: The contents of the Final Degree Project carried out by each student individually will be framed within one of the work topics included in the area of Engineering in which they have completed their studies, as indicated in the objectives of each degree.

assessment_methods.method: Monitoring of the student's in-person activities by their academic tutor
Final document presented by the student
Public presentation of the work before the tribunal and subsequent debate with it

assessment_rules: The final definition of the Final Degree Project evaluation system will conform to the regulations defined in the Final Degree Regulations of the School of Engineering. Both ordinary and extraordinary evaluations are carried out through a public presentation before a tribunal of three professors from the School. Although the Final Degree Project may be part of a joint work, the presentation must be individual, clearly indicating the particular aspects or contribution of each student to the whole.
